independent.summary: A column whose unquoted name is in TABLE_CONSTRAINTS is silently discarded. `looksLikeTableConstraint` (:341) returns true for any bare word in that set, and `readTableConstraint` then returns null for PERIOD/EXCLUDE/FULLTEXT/SPATIAL, so the `if (!constraint) continue` at :571 drops the definition with no drop reason. `CREATE TABLE budgets (id int PRIMARY KEY, period date NOT NULL, amount numeric);` proposes a Data Store with only `id` and `amount` — `period` vanishes and the reviewer is never told. `KEY`/`INDEX` got a TYPE_WORDS guard for exactly this collision; these keywords (none of them reserved in Postgres) did not.

`readAlterTableForeignKeys` mines a trailing ALTER only for `FOREIGN KEY`, but a real `pg_dump --schema-only` emits PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE the same way (`ALTER TABLE ONLY x ADD CONSTRAINT x_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id);`) and never inline — so against the headline input no column ever carries a `PRIMARY KEY` or `UNIQUE` marker, contradicting docs/api.md ("valued with its type plus `PRIMARY KEY`, `NOT NULL` and `UNIQUE` as declared"). The gap is hidden by the fixture: `server/tests/fixtures/schema.sql` is headed "Taken with: pg_dump --schema-only" yet writes its keys as inline `CONSTRAINT … PRIMARY KEY (id)` / `UNIQUE (email)`, a form pg_dump does not produce, so no test covers the shape the producer is sold on.

An unclosed `(` makes `statements()` merge the whole rest of the file into one statement, because depth never returns to 0 so no later `;` splits. `CREATE TABLE a (id int;` followed by twenty valid `CREATE TABLE`s yields exactly one drop reason — `CREATE TABLE "a" … its column list is not closed` — and every subsequent table is lost with nothing said, where the header promises an unreadable construct is "reported rather than silently reading half a schema".

`#` is treated as a line comment unconditionally, but it is an operator character in Postgres. A generated column or CHECK using a jsonb path operator — `payload jsonb, name text GENERATED ALWAYS AS (payload #>> '{name}') STORED` — has everything from `#` to end of line dropped by the lexer, which loses the closing parens and commas of that line; the column list then fails to balance and the whole table is dropped (or, per the finding above, every table after it).
